heading: Fields that Needs fills
body: Put Needs on each field that the container fills, and write no constructor. The container is the part of Tachyon that creates providers and fills fields. The spelling is @Needs in JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, Groovy, Kotlin and Dart. It is [Needs] in C#, [<Needs>] on a settable property in F# (an F# primary constructor parameter works too), #[Needs] in PHP, Rust and Ruby, // @Needs in Go and -- @Needs in Lua, where the field is written `order_store = nil,` in the class table. Put it above a field of the managed class or struct. The field must be direct, uninitialized (it has no starting value) and non-static. It must not be nullable either, because the container never fills it with null: the build refuses `store?: OrderStore`, `store: OrderStore | None`, `Optional[OrderStore]`, `?OrderStore $store`, `Option<Arc<OrderStore>>` and a Kotlin, Dart or C# `OrderStore?` with TY1331. Write `store!: OrderStore` in TypeScript, `lateinit var store: OrderStore` in Kotlin and `late final OrderStore store;` in Dart. The same rule holds for every field of a NeedsAll class that has no starting value. The field name uses the language's own variable case, not the class name. It is `orderStore` in JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Groovy, Kotlin, Dart and Go, and `$orderStore` in PHP. It is `order_store` in Python, Ruby, Lua and Rust. In C#, a private field is `_orderStore`, and a property or a public field is `OrderStore`. The build refuses `OrderStore OrderStore;` or a Python `orderStore` with TY1332. Only the case is checked, so a field `ledger` with Named("OrderStore") stays allowed. Tachyon assigns the marked fields in the order you declare them. Tachyon leaves an unmarked field alone. Typed languages require the exact concrete provider type. Rust requires Arc<Provider> or std::sync::Arc<Provider>. Go requires *Provider or Provider. JavaScript matches the field to the exact lowerCamel name of the provider (MoneyService becomes moneyService, CatalogClient becomes catalogClient). It rejects any match that is ambiguous. Fields with a starting value and static state stay unchanged. There is no hidden Setting or configuration binding. When the field itself does not select a provider, Named("Provider") names it directly. If that name matches no provider in the entry scope, the build fails. Lifetime still chooses singleton, request or transient. Controllers use request by default, and providers use singleton by default. All of them are local to one invocation. This feature does not give Tac a dependency injection (DI) container. Tac keeps its behavior contexts, which your code owns and creates.
